sections.title: Creeping growth
sections.text: Stenocereus eruca, the creeping devil cactus, is a prostrate cactus endemic to sandy coastal ground in Baja California Sur, Mexico. Its cylindrical stems lie along the ground, usually only their growing tips rising; stems can reach about 3 m long and 7–8 cm thick.

sections.title: Stems, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The green stems have ribs and stout spines, and root along their underside as they extend; older rear portions may die. Nocturnal flowers are cream-yellow, about 10–12 cm long and 8–10 cm wide. The ripe fruits are globose, red and spiny, about 3–4 cm across.

sections.title: Ecology and plate
sections.text: The plate shows the low, sprawling stems, flower and red fruit described for this species. It is documented as a narrow regional endemic; no food use is included because the consulted botanical sources did not establish one.
